conflicts.description: The Tithe Lamp seeks to renegotiate the Pact and own the air outright, while the Pale Mitre insists its oaths grant them sovereign control, pushing the city toward open scheming and sabotage.
conflicts.name: The Air Rights Dispute

conflicts.description: The Ringers conceal that the bell's tides are weakening, and both rival powers court or coerce them to learn the truth before the air runs out.
conflicts.name: The Secret of the Bell

description: Far below the surface, at the bottom of a lightless trench, lies the Cathedral of Saint Verrow, a colossal Gothic structure swallowed by the sea centuries ago. Its sealed stone vaults now hold air, and an entire city has grown inside and around the cathedral, with its nave serving as the main thoroughfare, its transepts as districts, and its buttresses as docks for pressure-hulled trade vessels. This is a mysterious, adult fantasy world of whispered bargains, where merchant houses and hereditary nobles scheme for control of the cathedral's dwindling breathable air and the glowing bell-tides that govern the city's life. Light comes from bioluminescent stained glass tended by guilds, and the cathedral itself seems to listen. Secrets drift like silt, debts are paid in breath, and every alliance hides a knife.

factions.description: The wealthiest merchant consortium, controlling the trade in compressed air and the pressure-hulled ships that link the city to the trench walls.
factions.name: House of the Tithe Lamp

factions.description: A coalition of noble families who claim descent from the cathedral's last bishops and rule by ritual precedent and inherited oaths.
factions.name: Court of the Pale Mitre

factions.description: A secretive order that tends the great bell and alone understands its tides. They sell silence and favors to both sides.
factions.name: Ringers of the Deep

history.description: The cathedral and its surrounding city sank into the trench in a single night, sealing thousands inside its vaults.
history.name: The Drowning

history.description: The bell tolled on its own, shifting the water and revealing the first breathable air pockets that saved the survivors.
history.name: The First Bell-Tide

history.description: Merchants and nobles signed a fragile accord dividing air rights, trading political power for the funding of the glass guilds.
history.name: The Pact of the Lamp

history.description: The bell fell quiet for a hundred years, and the city survived on hoarded air and growing desperation, until it tolled again without explanation.
history.name: The Silent Century

locations.description: The vast central hall of the drowned cathedral, now a lamplit market avenue beneath a vaulted ceiling hung with brine-stained banners. Merchants hawk air-salt, pearl-lenses and sealed letters between the pillars.
locations.name: The Nave Concourse

locations.description: The cathedral's eastern end, where luminous stained-glass windows glow with captive deep-sea creatures. The noble courts hold their audiences here, bathed in shifting colored light.
locations.name: The Choir of Glass

locations.description: A flooded undercroft beneath the cathedral's tower where the great bell hangs in black water. Its tolling shifts the currents and breathable air, and smugglers and heretics hide among the tombs.
locations.name: The Bellwell Crypt

name: The Drowned Nave

rules.statement: Breathable air is rationed by the bell-tide and is the true basis of all debt; a person's standing is measured in the breath they owe or are owed.
Only consecrated cathedral stone resists the trench's crushing pressure; any structure built from other material beyond the walls implodes within a season.
When the great bell tolls, the water in the cathedral shifts and air pockets migrate; no one knows if the bell responds to the Ringers or to something older.
Violence within the cathedral's sanctified nave is forbidden by ancient oath, so rivals resort to contracts, poisons, and proxies.
Stained-glass windows hold living light-creatures that record what is spoken near them, and guilds sell this testimony as evidence.
